frames.label: Current authority
frames.note: Most capabilities remain under legacy or human authority. Coupling and unknowns are explicit.

frames.label: Seam identified
frames.note: The operational and assignment seam is bounded. Dependencies, evidence, and rollback are named before routing changes.

frames.label: Shadow / dual-run
frames.note: The candidate mirrors or receives bounded traffic while legacy remains authoritative and rollback stays available.

frames.label: Validated authority
frames.note: Authority transfers only for the validated capability. Risky, coupled, human, and unknown work remains deliberately visible.

lenses.label: Authority topology
lenses.note: Locate execution and decision authority without treating position as value, maturity, effort, safety, or priority.

lenses.label: Assurance gates
lenses.note: Seven independent evidence gates surround the transfer. Their categories are research-backed; applicability and pass/fail remain product-specific.

lenses.label: Runtime + data
lenses.note: Read, write, response, record, authorization, comparison, and fallback relationships are distinct. Shadow never implies stateful safety.

lenses.label: Recovery + retirement
lenses.note: A cutover is followed by observation, rollback holding, controlled stop, retention, and owner authorization before decommission.

lenses.label: Evidence provenance
lenses.note: Every broadened assertion exposes source class, boundary, disconfirmation, and the evidence that could change the decision.

capabilities.label: Profiles, permissions & case assignment
capabilities.evidence: Historical source assertion; first bounded candidate

capabilities.label: Variant detail views and status rules

assuranceGates.label: Regulatory + intended-use context
assuranceGates.summary: Research or clinical; display or recommend; HCP or patient; time-critical or deliberative; established or uncertain genomic relevance.
assuranceGates.boundary: External guidance cannot determine device status, intended use, jurisdiction, or pathway for this system.

assuranceGates.label: Clinical evidence
assuranceGates.summary: Keep valid clinical association, analytical validation, and clinical validation distinct.
assuranceGates.boundary: May sit outside a bounded operational capability if it has no clinical interpretation or patient-facing effect.

assuranceGates.label: Software evidence bundle
assuranceGates.summary: Requirements; interfaces and data flows; traceability; configuration; test results; anomalies; rollback.
assuranceGates.boundary: The exact documentation level depends on intended use, risk, and applicable pathway.

assuranceGates.label: Human-factors critical-task delta
assuranceGates.summary: Perception, cognition, physical interaction, and critical-task sequence changes; URRA and validation method.
assuranceGates.boundary: A documented assessment may show no UI or critical-task delta for the bounded change.

assuranceGates.label: Safety + cybersecurity
assuranceGates.summary: Safety hazards; threat model; trust boundaries; SBOM; testing; logging; recovery; patchability; ownership.
assuranceGates.boundary: Cyber-device obligations are conditional; generic security architecture remains relevant but is not compliance proof.

assuranceGates.label: Records, audit + genomic custody
assuranceGates.summary: Actor, authority, action, time, reason, prior/resulting state, source version, retention, access, recovery, data-use limits.
assuranceGates.boundary: Part 11, HIPAA, CLIA, and NIH controlled-access applicability require separate scope determinations.

assuranceGates.label: Change authorization
assuranceGates.summary: Intended-use change; new risk; pathway rationale; HF and security impact; approvers; release criteria; monitoring; rollback trigger.
assuranceGates.boundary: A bounded non-device operational change may need a smaller evidence set, but must still preserve authority, audit, and rollback semantics.

migrationGates.label: Seam readiness
migrationGates.summary: Stable identity; routable interception or abstraction; owner and dependency map; known system of record.

migrationGates.label: Data readiness
migrationGates.summary: Backfill scope; schema compatibility; lag; conflicts; reconciliation; idempotency.

migrationGates.label: Contract readiness
migrationGates.summary: Declared interface; current provider verification; failure behavior; version compatibility.

migrationGates.label: Runtime readiness
migrationGates.summary: Canary/control separation; user-centered indicators; adequate window; parity and error-budget verdict.

migrationGates.label: Security readiness
migrationGates.summary: Per-request authorization equivalence; least privilege; audience and scope; telemetry boundary.

migrationGates.label: Authority transfer
migrationGates.summary: Rollback rehearsed; residual risk reviewed; named domain, operations, quality, and security authorization.

migrationGates.label: Retirement readiness
migrationGates.summary: No unresolved dependencies; controlled stop; archive retrieval; retention and owner approvals; temporary controls retired.

runtimeItems.label: Interception router / abstraction
runtimeItems.summary: A routable seam or branch-by-abstraction boundary separates candidate behavior without asserting that the domain is already separable.
runtimeItems.boundary: Proxy, ACL, bottleneck, and unclear-domain risks remain.

runtimeItems.label: Legacy execution + decision authority
runtimeItems.summary: Legacy serves the authoritative result until the named gate authorizes a bounded transfer.
runtimeItems.boundary: Physical deployment does not itself define authority.

runtimeItems.label: Target implementation
runtimeItems.summary: In F2 it may receive non-authoritative mirrored traffic; in F3 only the evidenced operational capability is shown as authoritative.
runtimeItems.boundary: No broader clinical, scientific, data-store, or retirement authority is implied.

runtimeItems.label: Contract + response comparator
runtimeItems.summary: Declared contract, current provider verification, and old/new result comparison are different evidence objects.
runtimeItems.boundary: Passing contracts does not replace data, security, production, or end-to-end evidence.

runtimeItems.label: Data transition + reconciliation
runtimeItems.summary: Backfill, outbox/CDC, idempotent consumption, lag, conflicts, and parity require explicit evidence if state moves.
runtimeItems.boundary: Uncoordinated dual writes are not assumed; CDC is not complete replication.

runtimeItems.label: Policy decision + enforcement
runtimeItems.summary: Authentication and authorization remain explicit at each protected resource; they do not move implicitly with a cube.
runtimeItems.boundary: Product-specific identity topology and policies were not available.

runtimeItems.label: Provenance + audit ledger
runtimeItems.summary: Record entities, activities, agents, derivations, versions, observations, decisions, and accountable owners.
runtimeItems.boundary: A provenance model does not itself establish retention, Part 11, HIPAA, or clinical-record applicability.

runtimeItems.label: Cohort, promotion + rollback controls
runtimeItems.summary: Cohort and traffic selection support evidence-bounded promotion and reversible rollback; temporary controls need retirement.
runtimeItems.boundary: Applicable two-, four-, six-, or eight-stage profile remains an internal decision.

discrepancies.question: Does generic shadow hide distinct read, write, response, and record-authority transitions here?
discrepancies.falsifier: Internal contracts and data flows show that the capability is stateless or that all authority dimensions move atomically.

discrepancies.question: Does validated authority need post-release stabilization and retirement readiness?
discrepancies.confidence: Medium—independent migration and retirement sources concur.
discrepancies.falsifier: The artifact is explicitly scoped only to pre-retirement authority and links to a separately governed retirement model.

discrepancies.question: Do all seven regulated-assurance gates apply to the operational capability?
discrepancies.falsifier: A documented applicability assessment places one or more gates outside the product or record boundary.
